injection_interface.account_credentials: The runner creates random passwords and receives access tokens in process memory only; stable localparts/device names are nonsecret fixture identity.
injection_interface.permissions: scripts/synapse-integration.sh sets umask 077 before creating runtime files.

credential_contract.redaction: Commands and evidence may emit only lane/phase, bounded counts, safe error category, exit status, and cleanup result. Passwords, tokens, keys, secrets, Matrix IDs, event bodies, and absolute user paths are forbidden.
credential_contract.rotation: Each reset destroys runtime files, Compose volumes, database/media/store state, and in-memory tokens; each setup generates fresh random credential material.
credential_contract.ci_rule: CI passes credentials only through the named runtime-file/process-memory interface; it never uses command-line arguments, committed values, job output, logs, or artifacts for usable secrets.

disposable_synapse.teardown_semantics: always/finally; cleanup failure is a separate failed result and no live evidence is valid
disposable_synapse.reset_postcondition: No Compose volume/orphan/database/media/generated config/key/credential/runtime child remains except integration/synapse/runtime/.gitkeep.

network_failure_controls.procedure: Block the client-to-Synapse loopback route for exactly 15 seconds while Synapse remains healthy.
network_failure_controls.expected: Client reports offline, owns no duplicate sync task, and converges after restoration.

network_failure_controls.procedure: Restart only the Synapse container after a recorded sync boundary.
network_failure_controls.expected: Bounded retry occurs without credential logging, lost acknowledged events, or duplicate timeline rows.

network_failure_controls.procedure: Terminate the test client after store flush and before the next sync token is acknowledged, then reopen the same disposable store.
network_failure_controls.expected: Exactly one owner resumes; state converges or fails explicitly without silent data loss.

fixtures.producer: future implementation in synara/scripts/run-synapse-two-client-integration.mjs; current runner bytes do not implement FX-64-CONTROL-v2
setup_procedure: Reset and start disposable Synapse through SYNARA-DISPOSABLE-RUNTIME-SECRETS-V1.
Create SENDER and synara_reader with fresh in-memory passwords; login READER-A and READER-B with exact device display names.
SENDER creates ROOM-CONTROL then ROOM-BOUNDARY, applies the exact membership/power state, and sends each 64-event corpus sequentially with acknowledged event IDs held only in memory.
Wait until both reader devices observe exactly 2 joined rooms and 128 unique ordered message events.
validation_assertions: Exactly 2 joined rooms, 0 spaces, and 128 message events exist; state events are excluded from the message count.
ROOM-CONTROL limited initial sync excludes index 0; context centered on index 32 returns it once; backward pagination prepends through index 0; latest is index 63.
ROOM-BOUNDARY m.read targets index 31, m.fully_read targets index 32, and m.read.private targets index 63; the second device converges according to receipt privacy semantics.
No duplicate, missing, cross-room, or out-of-order event is accepted; sender/room/event/device IDs and bodies remain absent from evidence.
fixtures.reset_teardown: Mandatory disposable_synapse.teardown after every pass/fail/timeout; rerun with the same seed recreates identities/shape but fresh credentials and Matrix IDs.

fixtures.producer: future fixture owner using the common reset/setup/send/wait/validate/teardown procedure
fixtures.validation: READER-A joins by public room alias, sees exactly 64 unique ordered events, and reset leaves only .gitkeep.

fixtures.producer: future E2EE fixture owner using the common reset/setup/send/wait/validate/teardown procedure
fixtures.validation: Both reader devices decrypt exactly 1000 ordered events, paginate to index 0, close/reopen the encrypted store, and retain no plaintext in evidence.

fixtures.producer: future large-account fixture owner using the common reset/setup/send/wait/validate/teardown procedure
fixtures.space_graph: SPACE-LARGE contains rooms 000..199 in numeric order; every tenth room is encrypted.
fixtures.validation: READER-A sees exactly one space, 200 joined rooms, 20 encrypted rooms, 1000 ordered events in ROOM-LARGE-000, and one event in each remaining room.

fixtures.producer: future media fixture owner using deterministic byte generation and the common lifecycle procedure
fixtures.validation: Both assets upload/download in both rooms with exact byte count and digest equality; cache reopen is bounded; bytes, MXC IDs, and keys are absent from evidence.

fixtures.producer: future reliability fixture owner using NF-OFFLINE-15 and the common lifecycle procedure
fixtures.validation: Each room converges to exactly 64 ordered events; index 31 precedes the gap, indices 32..51 are sent offline, index 52 is first post-gap, and no duplicate sync owner or stale-generation update survives.

evidence_lifecycle.binding: Every produced lane record names exact base/head SHA, producer command/procedure, result, platform, fixture/counts, sanitized artifact path or immutable URL, owner, independent reviewer, captured_at, expiry/refresh triggers, dependencies, and explicit exclusions.
evidence_lifecycle.failure_rule: Failed, blocked, rejected, deferred, stale, expired, missing, or merely produced evidence remains gate-open. Cleanup failure invalidates the live result.
evidence_lifecycle.refresh_rule: Live/performance evidence expires after seven UTC days; toolchain evidence refreshes on toolchain/lock changes; ephemeral evidence expires with its artifact; every row refreshes on candidate-head, fixture, producer, SDK, Synapse image, platform, or acceptance-criteria change.
